web_evidence.title: The Lucky One by Nicholas Sparks — Excerpt
web_evidence.note: Publisher-authorized sustained opening narrates Clayton and Thibault externally while presenting their perceptions and thoughts. Dialogue is clearly distinguished from narration.

web_evidence.title: Nicholas Sparks — The Lucky One Writing Notes
web_evidence.note: The author explicitly describes the novel as limited third person, explaining that character-centered chapters restrict access to the focal character's thoughts. Changing perspectives concerns focalization, not grammatical person.

search_log: Read TASK.md, PERSON_METHODOLOGY.md, PROMPT.md, book.json, quotes.csv, and result_schema.json. Referenced companion METHODOLOGY.md was absent.
Searched: Nicholas Sparks The Lucky One excerpt chapter; The Lucky One Nicholas Sparks third person point of view.
Opened the publisher-authorized ReadingGroupGuides excerpt and the author's whole-book writing notes.
Searched title plus distinctive first-person phrases: Every now and then / meet a guy; I got the sense / marry him; I overlooked some obvious.

Follow-up searches used Sparks plus I overlooked some obvious problems; I knew it wasn’t fair / anger; I got the sense that he was the kind; Every now and then / plague. Results supplied quote aggregations or irrelevant matches, not reliable surrounding dialogue context.
person_note: THIRD: sustained Goodreads scenes agree with the authorized opening, and Sparks explicitly confirms third-person narration with changing character focalization throughout the novel. First-person confessions are interpreted as local speech, not autonomous narrative sections; several event buckets may therefore contain dialogue. Exact attribution remains uncertain for some clipped passages, especially q01775 and q01782, but there is no credible evidence of sustained changes in narrative person.
